result.title: The KL Divergence Is Never Negative, Except in PyTorch
result.summary: A Kullback--Leibler (KL) divergence is never negative, yet PyTorch users have reported negative values for years, and the standard advice is to clamp them at zero. The sign is only the visible part of a silent failure. Many machine-learning applications compare nearby distributions, where conventional KL formulas lose accuracy. On 8.5 million inputs with certified references across 18 closed-form KL families and F.kl_div, we find widespread errors in values and gradients on CPU and GPU. Among scalar families in ordinary parameter ranges, over 85% of FP32 values have at least 1% relative error near KL 10^(-7) (FP16: 10^(-3)), and about 30% become negative at smaller divergences. More precision is not the cure: evaluated one precision higher, the same formulas still leave 7--51% of FP32 values significantly wrong for 22 of 23 configurations. Stable closed-form decompositions, compensated arithmetic, and analytic gradients remove over 97% of significant errors in the working format. Strict repairs eliminate significant errors on 7.2 million scored closed-form samples and correctly round all 567 million scored F.kl_div components. The errors affect parameter fitting, Bayesian decisions, identical-start distillation (up to 97% top-1 disagreement), KL-based layer rankings in a quantized LLM, and 19--59% of GPT-2 circuit edge scores. With the repaired code they all but vanish. Code and data: https://github.com/xi-xiaoran/stablekl

AI.brief_summary: 论文在 850 万条带认证参考的输入上系统检验 PyTorch 中 18 类闭式 KL 族与 F.kl_div 的数值值与梯度误差（CPU/GPU、FP32/FP16），并给出稳定闭式分解、补偿算术与解析梯度等修复方案，可消除 97% 以上的显著误差。
AI.relevance_reason: 若 LVR 训练以 KL 正则、近邻分布蒸馏或 KL 作 latent 状态相似度与贡献排序，其实现误差可能污染梯度与排序，文中稳定分解与解析梯度可供核查；但与视觉推理主线无直接联系。
